label: rem:markov-gram-bilinear-vs-star
title: Two pairings, two signatures: $\mathrm{tr}_M(b_ib_j)$ versus $\mathrm{tr}_M(b_ib_j^{*})$
html:
The normal-form basis of H_3(q) admits two Gram matrices, and they do not have the same signature. Which one is meant has to be said.

The bilinear pairing

Dropping the star and pairing G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) gives, block by block, the bilinear trace form \mathrm{tr}(AB) on each matrix algebra. Parametrise A \in M_2 by its symmetric part (\alpha,\delta,\beta) and its antisymmetric part \gamma, so that

  A \;=\; \begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \beta+\gamma \\ \beta-\gamma & \delta \end{pmatrix}.

Then

  \mathrm{tr}(A^{2}) \;=\; \alpha^{2} \;+\; 2\beta^{2} \;-\; 2\gamma^{2} \;+\; \delta^{2}.

Three squares enter with a plus sign and one with a minus, and the symmetric and antisymmetric parts are orthogonal, so \mathrm{tr}(AB) on M_d has signature \bigl(\tfrac{d(d+1)}{2},\, \tfrac{d(d-1)}{2}\bigr). Summing over the blocks with y_\lambda > 0 reproduces the whole signature of G: convention C gives (5,1,0) and convention D gives (4,1,1).

The negative direction is identified rather than measured. It is the antisymmetric element E_{12} - E_{21} of the M_2 sitting in the (2,1) block --- the rotation generator of \mathfrak{sl}_2. Any algebra with a two-dimensional irrep contributes one such direction, so G is indefinite for every q and for every convention with y_{(2,1)} > 0. The indefiniteness is a property of the pairing, not of the substrate.

The star pairing, and what is withdrawn

An earlier reading took the single negative eigenvalue of G as a physical signature: the trace pairing was said to be a spacetime form, and the framework's natural object a causal structure rather than a metric space. That reading is withdrawn. A metric is built from the *-structure, and the Hecke *-structure is T_w^{*} = T_{w^{-1}}. Pairing against it replaces the bilinear \mathrm{tr}(AB) by the sesquilinear \mathrm{tr}(AB^{*}), which on M_d is a sum of d^{2} squares: signature (d^{2},0), no negative direction anywhere. The eigenvalue magnitudes are unchanged --- the star flips exactly the sign of the antisymmetric direction, which is what a *-structure is for --- and the sign flip is what the star form's positivity records.

The bilinear analysis is retained because it is the same block decomposition that explains both answers. It is the interpretation that was wrong, not the arithmetic.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. Under the bilinear pairing at q_0 the eigenvalues are -0.855067,\, 0.101797,\, 0.855067^{\times 3},\, 3.476950 for convention C and -0.752702,\, 0,\, 0.752702^{\times 3},\, 4.230339 for convention D, where \det G = 2.89 \times 10^{-51}, i.e. zero at 50 decimal places. Under the star pairing every one of those magnitudes recurs with a positive sign.
